title: Composition and affine examples of adequately affine morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal U\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal V\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal W$ be morphisms of algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. If $f$ and $g$ are adequately affine [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism], then $g\circ f$ is adequately affine. Moreover, every affine morphism of algebraic stacks is adequately affine. Here affine means representable by schemes with affine scheme morphisms after every scheme base change: for every $T\to\mathcal V$ with $T$ a scheme, $\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T$ is a scheme and the inverse image of each affine open of $T$ is affine [def-pc-scheme]. No finite-type or characteristic assumption is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(1),(2), printed p.20; composition and affine examples. Primary arXiv:1005.2398v3 read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism], $f$ and $g$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-composition-affine] to obtain both properties for $h=g\circ f$. Fix an arbitrary surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal U$. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image], $\mathcal C=f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal D=f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal B$ are quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal V$ whose smooth-etale restrictions are $f_*\mathcal A$ and $f_*\mathcal B$. Adequate affineness of $f$ makes $\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ universally adequate; it need not be surjective.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(1),(2), with Lemma 4.1.7 for composition; printed pp.17--20; https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S4.SS2

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-algebra-pushforward] to the adequately affine map $g$ and the universally adequate map $\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. It gives universal adequacy of $g_*\mathcal C\to g_*\mathcal D$. The natural algebra composition isomorphism in [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image] identifies this map with $h_*\mathcal A\to h_*\mathcal B$, including its maps on every smooth test. Since the surjection was arbitrary and $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] proves that $h$ is adequately affine.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(1),(2), with Lemma 4.1.7 for composition; printed pp.17--20; https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S4.SS2

proof.text: Now let $q:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ be affine in the stated sense. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-composition-affine], $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For any quasi-coherent algebra surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$, [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image] gives a surjection $q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal B$. By the smooth-chart and surjection comparisons of [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image], this is $q_*\mathcal A\to q_*\mathcal B$ on the smooth-etale site, and each target section lifts after an etale covering. Taking exponent $1$ gives precisely universal adequacy. Thus [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] makes $q$ adequately affine.
